L87: ### Theorem 1
L88: 
L89: Let G be a countable (finite or infinite) group. Then, there is a hyperbolic Riemann surface X and a family of dessins \(\left\{ (X,\mathcal {D}_H)\right\} _{H\le G}\) such that,
L90: 
L91:   1. (i)
L92: 
L93: \(\mathrm{Isom}^{+}(X)\cong G\),
L94: 
L95:   2. (ii)
L96: 
L97: \(\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mathcal {D}_H)=\left\{ h\in \mathrm{Isom}^+(X)\ |\ h(\mathcal {D}_H)=\mathcal {D}_H\right\} \cong H\),
L98: 
L99:   3. (iii)
L100: 
L101: \(H_1\le H_2\ \Longrightarrow \ \mathcal {D}_{H_1}\le \mathcal {D}_{H_2}\).
L102: Furthermore, if G is finite, then X can be chosen compact so obtaining a family of Grothendieck dessins.
L103: In [【35†10】], it was observed that, given a topological action of a finite group G on a compact surface X, there is a Grothendieck’s dessin \({\mathcal D}=(X,{\mathcal G})\) such that G induces \(\mathrm{Aut}({\mathcal D})\). This result states that not only there is a dessin with a given group of automorphisms, but also that the given topological action is preserved by the automorphism group.
L104: In particular, the strong symmetric genus of a finite group is also the minimal genus action at the level of Grothendieck’s dessins. The proof of such result was done in terms of Riemann surfaces, Fuchsian groups and quasiconformal deformation theory. In this paper, we provide a simple and short argument to the above realisation that also works for any countable group.
L105: ### Theorem 2
L106: 
L107: Let X be a surface and fix a topologically tame action \(\theta :G \rightarrow \mathrm{Hom}^{+}(X)\), where G is a countable (finite or infinite) group. Then there is a dessin \({\mathcal D}=(X,{\mathcal G})\) with \(\mathrm{Aut}({\mathcal D})\) isomorphic to G and induced by the topological action of \(\theta (G)\).
